selected.rationale: The Wellness Optimizer tracks sleep, supplements, and workouts with a low price sensitivity and an affinity for wellness categories, perfectly mirroring the advertiser's primary category of general wellness services and mid-to-high price tier.

The Fitness Enthusiast works out frequently and holds a strong category affinity for fitness services and recovery, aligning directly with the appointment-based booking and self-care offerings of the recommended publisher Studiogrid.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent focuses on kids' products, household items, and meal kits, which do not align with the core wellness services focus of the advertiser.
The Gen Z Aesthete is primarily focused on fashion, beauty, and functional beverages discovered on social media, whereas this advertiser offers general wellness services.
The Pet Parent focuses strictly on pet health, pet food, and pet supplies, which is entirely irrelevant to human wellness services.
The Affluent Classic gravitates towards classic apparel, travel, and home goods rather than active personal wellness services.
The Sustainability Buyer prioritizes eco-friendly apparel, clean beauty, and refillable products, which lacks a direct connection to general wellness services.
The Convenience-First Millennial is driven by instant delivery, meal kits, and quick commerce, which does not match the service-based nature of the advertiser.
The Value-Conscious Shopper looks for discounts and bundles on groceries and household goods, conflicting with the service orientation and estimated AOV of the advertiser.
The Gifter is a temporary mode centered on holiday or life event gifting with physical items like gift sets, which does not fit an ongoing service.
